source_title: Centre Cuts Cancer Drug Rates; Supreme Court Asks Why Cap Isn't Expanded - India Today - India Today
source_excerpt:
The central government has revised maximum retail prices for 543 anti-cancer drug brands following a 30 per cent trade margin cap imposed by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority, with generic and biosimilar medicines seeing cuts of up to 93 per cent taking effect from November 9. The Supreme Court has reserved its order while questioning the disparity between retailer costs and retail prices, asking why trade margin caps cannot be extended to other essential medicines. Meanwhile, the Karnataka government has mandated hospitals to disclose both purchase costs and maximum retail prices on patient bills from November 1 to improve billing transparency. Read More

Yamuna Water Quality Spark Political Row in Delhi Ahead of Chhath Puja
A political face-off has erupted in Delhi between the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Aam Aadmi Party over the Yamuna's water quality ahead of the festive season and Chhath Puja. BJP Member of Parliament Manoj Tiwari took a dip in the Yamuna and tasted its water, asserting that over half of the river has been cleaned in two years and daring former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal to take a dip. Rejecting the claim, the Aam Aadmi Party accused the BJP of misleading the public, maintaining that the Palla-Wazirabad stretch has always been relatively clean while challenging BJP leaders to drink water from the polluted Kalindi Kunj stretch instead.
India Inequality Hits Sharp Decline, Gini Index at 23.5: World Bank Report
According to the latest World Bank report, India's inequality has registered its sharpest decline in five years, recording a Gini index of 23.5 in 2026. This places India among low-inequality nations compared to China at 36 and the United States at 42. Extreme poverty in India has dropped from 27.6% to under 2.6%. Additionally, the proportion of the population living on under 400 rupees a day has decreased from 57.7% to 16.1%, reflecting rising consumption power despite inflationary pressures.
Election Commission Extends SIR Timelines in Delhi, Maharashtra and 4 States
The Election Commission has extended the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls schedule across Delhi, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Telangana, and Nagaland following requests from their respective Chief Electoral Officers. In Maharashtra, the deadline for filing claims and objections has moved to 13 November, with the final electoral roll to be published on 30 November. In Delhi, claims and objections can now be submitted until 25 November, with disposals pushed to 15 December and publication of the final roll set for 22 December to address logical discrepancies.
UP Tightens Job Rules, Bars Candidates Linked To Violent Regime Change Calls
The Uttar Pradesh government has revised character verification rules for government recruitment, barring candidates associated with organisations seeking regime change through violent means. Under the directives, participation in such activities within three years preceding verification, after turning 21, may lead to disqualification. The state clarified that political ideology alone cannot disqualify candidates, nor does a pending FIR or investigation automatically bar employment. Opposition parties have criticised the directive, alleging that the administration is attempting to suppress democratic protests and intimidate students and youth.
